children: Bitcoin has rallied more than 50% from its lows this year but remains down year to date, while short interest in several bitcoin-linked stocks remains elevated, keeping squeeze risk high, according to S3 Partners Director of Research Leon Gross.

have each shown return correlations above 0.70 with bitcoin, while their correlations with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were around 0.4, Gross said. That leaves the stocks with meaningful exposure to both bitcoin and broader equity markets.

The accompanying levels chart showed ASST as the standout, rising to roughly 190% of its January level by late September. MSTR also finished above its January baseline at around 110%, while COIN ended at roughly 88%. Bitcoin remained just below its January level at around 98%, despite its rebound from earlier lows.
Strategy held 846,000 bitcoin, equivalent to about 4% of bitcoin outstanding, and had a market capitalization of about $65B, according to S3.

Coinbase, whose revenue is directly linked to cryptocurrency transaction activity through commissions and other fees, had a $53B market capitalization. Strive had about $2B in assets under management, 26,355 bitcoin and a $3B market capitalization.

Short interest remained elevated across all three stocks. The short-interest chart showed MSTR and COIN at roughly 10% and 13% of float, respectively, toward the end of the period, while ASST's short interest was also elevated on its separate right-hand scale.

S3 said MSTR's and ASST's short interest had shown both positive and negative correlations with their stock prices at different times. COIN's relationship was mostly negative, although the correlation turned more positive as the stock rose in August. S3 said a positive correlation indicated investors were shorting the stocks as they moved higher.

Short interest in all three fell from mid-July into mid-August as the stocks rose, with COIN bottoming first before turning higher. The squeeze-score chart shows elevated readings across the group, with MSTR's score above 70 at times and ASST reaching 100 and remaining above 70 frequently.
ASST was the only one of the three to experience a squeeze in August, when its shares rose sharply as short interest declined while its squeeze score remained high.

S3 said ASST's smaller size and thinner following made it more susceptible to short covering, while MSTR and COIN, with market capitalizations of about $65B and $53B, respectively, were too large for short covering alone to move their shares in the same way.
Bitcoin ETF IBIT, meanwhile, had very little short interest and was not considered crowded. S3 said equity investors may be using MSTR, ASST, and COIN as proxies for short positions on bitcoin.

title: Bitcoin's rebound puts crowded crypto shorts on alert
